title: Novel SIM1 Variants Expanding the Spectrum of SIM1-Related Obesity.
authors: Mohammed, Idris; Ahmed, Wesam S; Al-Barazenji, Tara; Dauleh, Hajar; Love, Donald R; Hussain, Khalid
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过测序发现SIM1转录因子新变异，并用AlphaFold3结构建模评估其对蛋白互作的影响，虽涉及TF-DNA相关蛋白但未聚焦DNA结合机制，方法上仅用结构预测，属广义蛋白-DNA互作边缘应用。
abstract: Monogenic forms of severe early-onset obesity often involve genetic disruptions in the hypothalamic leptin-melanocortin pathway. Pathogenic variants in the SIM1 gene, a key transcription factor required for the development of the paraventricular nucleus, are a known cause of Prader-Willi-like syndrome, characterized by hyperphagia, severe obesity, and developmental delay. We performed targeted next-generation sequencing of 52 obesity-associated genes on a cohort of pediatric patients with severe early-onset obesity. Identified variants were analyzed for population frequency and predicted pathogenicity using in silico tools. The structural impact of the novel missense variants was assessed using protein domain modeling with AlphaFold3. We identified five rare SIM1 variants in eleven patients. Four were heterozygous nonsynonymous variants: one frameshift in the bHLH domain (p.Ser18Ter), one frameshift in the Per-ARNT-Sim domain (p.His143Ter), and two missense variants, p.Pro30Ala and p.Ser663Leu. Structural modeling suggested that the missense variants are likely to disrupt critical protein-protein interactions. The fifth variant was a synonymous change, c.1173G>A, p.(Ser391Ser), which was detected in five unrelated patients. Bioinformatic analysis predicted that this variant could alter splicing. Structural modeling suggested that the missense variants interfere with SIM1 function. This study expands the mutational spectrum of SIM1-linked monogenic obesity, reporting novel likely pathogenic frameshift variants, a missense variant, and a recurrent synonymous variant with a potential splice-site effect. The majority of the variants are predicted to affect the SIM1 protein. Our findings strengthen the critical role of the SIM1 gene in hypothalamic development and energy homeostasis. The results underscore the importance of including the SIM1 gene in genetic testing panels for children with severe obesity and hyperphagia, enabling precise diagnosis and potential future personalized management. Functional in vitro or in vivo validation of these variants is required to confirm their pathogenicity.
abstract_zh: 单基因形式的严重早发性肥胖通常涉及下丘脑瘦素-黑皮质素通路（leptin-melanocortin pathway）的遗传破坏。SIM1基因是室旁核发育所需的关键转录因子，其致病变异是导致Prader-Willi样综合征的已知原因，该综合征以食欲亢进、严重肥胖和发育迟缓为特征。我们对一组患有严重早发性肥胖的儿科患者进行了52个肥胖相关基因的靶向下一代测序。通过计算机工具对鉴定出的变异进行了群体频率分析和致病性预测。使用AlphaFold3进行蛋白质结构域建模，评估了新错义变异的结构影响。我们在十一名患者中鉴定出五个罕见的SIM1变异。其中四个为杂合非同义变异：一个位于bHLH结构域的移码变异（p.Ser18Ter），一个位于Per-ARNT-Sim结构域的移码变异（p.His143Ter），以及两个错义变异p.Pro30Ala和p.Ser663Leu。结构建模提示，这些错义变异可能破坏关键的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用。第五个变异为同义变异c.1173G>A，p.(Ser391Ser)，在五名无关患者中检测到。生物信息学分析预测该变异可能影响剪接。结构建模提示，这些错义变异干扰SIM1功能。本研究扩展了SIM1相关单基因肥胖的突变谱，报道了新的可能致病的移码变异、一个错义变异以及一个具有潜在剪接位点效应的复发性同义变异。大多数变异预计影响SIM1蛋白。我们的发现强化了SIM1基因在下丘脑发育和能量稳态中的关键作用。结果强调了在严重肥胖和食欲亢进儿童的基因检测组合中纳入SIM1基因的重要性，从而实现精准诊断和未来可能的个性化管理。需要对这些变异进行体外或体内功能验证，以确认其致病性。
